I would keep the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the most steady way for me to farm because I know the management well, the machinery fits it, and the weather pattern also fits it. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field from last autumn, so I would focus first on managing wheat carefully through spring with fertilizer, irrigation, and disease control, then harvest it in early summer and go straight into summer maize. At my age, I would not spread myself across too many crops. I would rather plant the crops I understand well, keep the field work simple, and aim for stable yield instead of taking extra market risk.

I would use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed. For wheat, I would use moderate fertilizer, about three irrigations, and a few pesticide sprays to control aphids, rust, and weeds if needed. After harvest, I would seed summer maize quickly to catch moisture and protect yield. For maize, I would use hybrid seed, put most fertilizer at the start with some later management, irrigate less than wheat, and keep pesticide use limited but timely for armyworm, corn borer, and leaf disease if they show up. I would mostly use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and matches local machinery. My goal would be steady grain output and lower management trouble over the whole year.
